- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.

g.passage: The bdelloid rotifer, a microscopic freshwater animal that has apparently reproduced without males for tens of millions of years, survives droughts in an unusual way______ expelling nearly all the water from its body and curling into a dormant, seedlike form that biologists call a tun.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격 삽입구를 지나면 주절 'The bdelloid rotifer ... survives droughts in an unusual way'가 완전한 독립절임을 알 수 있다. 빈칸 뒤 'expelling ... a tun'은 주어와 동사가 없는 분사구로, 앞의 'unusual way'가 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명한다. 독립절 뒤에 설명을 덧붙일 때는 콜론을 쓰므로 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론과 D의 마침표는 뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데, 분사구만 있어 틀린 문장이 된다. C의 ', and'는 두 개의 독립절이나 대등한 요소를 이어야 하지만, 뒤에 대등하게 연결될 절이 없어 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: Once you look past the long appositive, you can see that the main clause, "The bdelloid rotifer ... survives droughts in an unusual way," is a complete independent clause. What follows the blank, "expelling ... a tun," is a participial phrase with no subject or verb of its own. It explains what the "unusual way" is. A colon correctly introduces this kind of explanation after an independent clause, so A is correct. B (a semicolon) and D (a period) both need an independent clause after the blank, but only a phrase follows, so they leave a fragment. C (", and") would need a parallel clause or element to join, and the text after the blank has none, so it is also incorrect.
g.design: A long appositive separates the subject from its verb, so students must first confirm that the main clause is complete. Then they must notice that the text after the blank is a participial phrase, not a clause. This rules out the semicolon, the period, and the ", and" option, all of which seem plausible at first.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.

g.passage: The narrator of Imogen Hale's novel The Lamplighter's Ledger—a widowed clerk who records every visitor to a fog-bound coastal inn—rarely comments on what he ______ he simply lists names, arrival times, and the condition of each guest's boots, leaving readers to infer the drama for themselves.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 대시로 둘러싸인 동격 삽입구를 빼고 보면 "The narrator ... rarely comments on what he sees"가 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "he simply lists ..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 틀렸다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the appositive between the dashes, you get "The narrator ... rarely comments on what he sees," which is an independent clause. The part after the blank, "he simply lists ...," is also an independent clause because it has its own subject and verb. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so B is the answer. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C correctly uses the conjunction "and," but it adds an unnecessary comma after "and." D has no punctuation at all, so the two clauses run together as a run-on sentence.
g.design: This is a medium question that takes two steps. First, students must look past the long appositive between the dashes to find the main clause. Then they must see that the text after the blank is also an independent clause. Distractor C looks partly correct because it uses a conjunction, but its extra comma makes it wrong.

g.passage: The Okavango Delta in Botswana is unusual among the world's large deltas: rather than emptying into an ocean, its waters spread across the Kalahari Desert and largely evaporate. The annual flood, fed by rains that fall months earlier in the Angolan highlands roughly 1,000 kilometers to the ______ the delta during the region's dry season, when wildlife from the surrounding arid lands converges on its channels and lagoons.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The annual flood"이고 동사는 "reaches"이다. 그 사이의 "fed by ... to the northwest"는 앞쪽 쉼표로 시작된 비필수 수식어이므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론 뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데 "reaches the delta..."에는 주어가 없어 틀리다. B는 "and"가 연결할 앞의 동사가 없고 주어와 동사 사이에 불필요한 접속사를 넣었으므로 틀리다. D는 수식어를 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 문장 구조가 흐트러진다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The annual flood," and its verb is "reaches." The phrase "fed by ... to the northwest" between them is a nonessential modifier that opens with a comma, so it must also close with a comma. That makes C correct. A is wrong because a semicolon must be followed by an independent clause, and "reaches the delta..." has no subject. B is wrong because there is no earlier verb for "and" to join, so it puts an unneeded conjunction between the subject and verb. D is wrong because it leaves out the comma that closes the modifier, which breaks the sentence structure.
g.design: 긴 분사 수식어가 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓아 독립절 경계처럼 보이게 했고, 세미콜론·접속사 오답이 그럴듯해 보이도록 만들었다.

g.passage: Before 1840, British postage was typically paid by the recipient and calculated according to distance and the number of sheets, a system that made ordinary correspondence a luxury. Rowland Hill, a former schoolmaster who had carefully studied the Post Office's actual costs, proposed a radical alternative______ a single low rate, prepaid by the sender with an adhesive stamp, would apply to any letter regardless of how far it traveled.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격구 'a former schoolmaster ... costs' 뒤에서도 주절은 'Rowland Hill ... proposed a radical alternative'로 완전한 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤 'a single low rate ... would apply ...'도 완전한 독립절이며 그 '대안'의 내용을 구체적으로 설명하므로, 앞 절을 부연하는 콜론(D)이 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 'which'를 넣으면 뒤에 이미 주어 'a single low rate'와 동사 'would apply'가 있어 관계절 구조가 성립하지 않는다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
g.explanation_en: Even with the long appositive phrase "a former schoolmaster ... costs" in the middle, the main clause "Rowland Hill ... proposed a radical alternative" is still a complete independent clause. The words after the blank, "a single low rate ... would apply ...," also form a complete independent clause, and that clause explains exactly what the alternative was, so a colon (D) is the right choice. Choice A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. Choice B adds "which," but the clause after it already has its own subject ("a single low rate") and verb ("would apply"), so it can't work as a relative clause. Choice C puts the two independent clauses together with no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구로 주절이 이미 끝났다는 점을 가린다. 그래서 학생은 독립절인지 판단한 뒤 뒤 절이 앞 절을 설명하는 관계인지도 확인해야 한다. 'which'와 쉼표는 언뜻 보면 맞는 것처럼 보이는 오답이다.

g.passage: The Falkirk Wheel, a boat lift that opened in Scotland in 2002, solved a long-standing problem for canal engineers. Two waterways sat 24 meters apart in height, and boats once needed most of a day to pass through a flight of eleven locks between them. The designers replaced that staircase of locks with a single rotating structure—two counterbalanced gondolas mounted on opposite arms of a central steel ______ because the gondolas always carry equal weights of water, turning the wheel takes remarkably little energy.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "two counterbalanced gondolas ... axle"는 대시로 시작한 삽입 설명(동격)이므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 하고, 그 뒤의 독립절 "turning the wheel takes..."는 앞 독립절과 등위접속사로 연결되어야 한다. A는 대시로 삽입구를 닫고 "and"로 두 절을 연결하므로 옳다. B는 "and"로 절은 연결하지만 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫아 부호가 짝을 이루지 않는다. C는 대시로 삽입구를 올바르게 닫지만 접속사가 없어 두 독립절이 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 세미콜론 뒤에 "and"를 써서 부호 쓰임이 비표준적이고, 대시로 연 삽입구도 닫히지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "two counterbalanced gondolas ... axle" is an appositive that opens with a dash, so it must close with a matching dash. After that, the independent clause "turning the wheel takes..." needs a coordinating conjunction to join it to the first clause. A does both: its dash closes the appositive, and "and" links the two independent clauses. B links the clauses correctly, but it closes a dash-opened interruption with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match. C closes the appositive correctly but has no conjunction, which leaves two independent clauses run together. D puts "and" after a semicolon, which is nonstandard here, and it never closes the dash.
g.design: To answer, students have to check two things: that the appositive opened with a dash is closed with a dash, and that the two independent clauses are joined. B and C each get one of these right, so students must compare them to rule them out.

g.passage: Ecologist Mariela Ortíz tracked how leafcutter ants in a Costa Rican forest respond when their underground fungus gardens are contaminated by a parasitic mold. Rather than abandoning the colony's chambers, specialized worker ants, the smallest members of the colony, physically remove infected fragments of fungus and carry them to distant refuse ______ they also coat healthy fungus with antimicrobial secretions produced by bacteria living on their bodies.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'specialized worker ants ... remove ... and carry them to distant refuse piles'는 독립절이고, 뒤의 'they also coat healthy fungus ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 절 사이를 잘못 끊는다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank ("specialized worker ants ... remove ... and carry them to distant refuse piles") is an independent clause, and the part after it ("they also coat healthy fungus ...") is also an independent clause because it has its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A connects the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between them at all, so you get a run-on sentence. D correctly adds the conjunction "and," but the extra comma after "and" doesn't belong there and wrongly splits the sentence.
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 동격 삽입구와 복합 동사구를 두어 절 경계를 흐리게 했고, 쉼표·무부호·'and' 뒤 불필요 쉼표 오답과 비교해야 세미콜론을 고를 수 있게 했다.

g.passage: In Marisol Okafor's 2019 novel The Lamplighter's Daughter, set in a fog-bound harbor town, the narrator, a widowed seamstress who keeps a careful ledger of every visitor to her rented rooms______ not only names and dates but also the weather on each day, a habit that gives the book the patient, gaslit texture of a Victorian serial.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "the narrator"이고 동사는 "records"이다. 그 사이에 "a widowed seamstress ... rooms"라는 비필수 동격어구가 쉼표로 시작되었으므로, 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 독립절 두 개를 연결할 때 쓰는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없어 독립절이 아니다. B는 동격어구를 닫는 쉼표가 없어 "rooms records"처럼 주어와 동사가 잘못 이어진다. D의 대시는 동격어구를 닫을 수는 있지만, 쉼표로 시작한 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 부호가 짝이 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "the narrator," and its verb is "records." Between them is a nonessential appositive ("a widowed seamstress ... rooms") that opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma as well. That makes C correct. A uses a semicolon, which joins two independent clauses, but the text before the blank has no main verb, so it is not an independent clause. B leaves out the closing comma, which runs the appositive straight into the verb ("rooms records"). D uses a dash, which can close an appositive, but an appositive that opens with a comma can't close with a dash because the punctuation has to match.
g.design: I placed a long nonessential appositive with an embedded relative clause between the subject and the verb. Students who skim may read the appositive as a complete clause and choose the semicolon, or they may miss the opening comma and choose the dash.

g.passage: The Okavango Delta—a vast inland wetland that, unlike most river deltas, forms where the Okavango River fans out across the dry Kalahari Basin______ empties into no ocean at all. Instead, nearly all of its water evaporates, is absorbed by plants, or seeps into the sand.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 'a vast inland wetland ... Kalahari Basin'은 주어 'The Okavango Delta'를 설명하는 비필수 동격 표현이고, 대시로 시작했으므로 대시로 닫아야 주어와 동사 'empties'가 바르게 이어집니다. 따라서 D가 정답입니다. B는 동격 안에 쉼표가 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫아 문장부호가 짝을 이루지 않습니다. A는 세미콜론 앞부분이 동사 없는 불완전한 구여서 독립절을 이어 주는 세미콜론을 쓸 수 없습니다. C는 삽입구를 닫는 문장부호가 없어 주어와 동격 표현의 경계가 드러나지 않습니다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a vast inland wetland ... Kalahari Basin" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject "The Okavango Delta." Because it opens with a dash, it must also close with a dash so the subject connects correctly to the verb "empties." That makes D the correct answer. B may look tempting because the appositive already contains commas, but it closes a dash-opened interruption with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match. A is wrong because the text before the semicolon is an incomplete phrase with no main verb, and a semicolon must join two independent clauses. C leaves out the closing punctuation, so nothing marks where the appositive ends.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구 안에 쉼표 삽입구를 넣어 쉼표 선택지를 유인으로 만들었다. 정답을 고르려면 여는 대시를 확인한 뒤 같은 대시로 닫아야 한다는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다.

g.passage: In 1871, Maejima Hisoka, a former government official who had carefully studied the British postal system, launched Japan's first public mail service between Tokyo and Osaka______ the network had expanded to more than five thousand post offices, linking remote farming villages to the nation's rapidly growing cities.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장에는 독립절이 두 개 있다("Maejima Hisoka ... launched ... Osaka"와 "the network had expanded ..."). A는 두 절을 세미콜론으로 구분하고, 도입구 "within a decade"를 쉼표로 둘째 절에 연결하므로 정답이다. B는 접속사 없이 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문법적으로 끊기는 것처럼 보이지만 "within a decade"를 1871년의 개통에 붙이게 되어, 첫 서비스 개통이 "10년 안에" 일어났다는 어색한 의미를 만들고, 이 구가 실제로 꾸며야 할 확장 시점과 분리된다. D는 두 독립절 사이에 문장부호가 전혀 없어 무종지문이 된다.
g.explanation_en: This sentence has two independent clauses: "Maejima Hisoka ... launched ... Osaka" and "the network had expanded ...." Choice A is correct because it puts a semicolon between the two clauses and uses a comma to attach the introductory phrase "within a decade" to the second clause. Choice B joins the two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. Choice C may look like it marks a proper break, but it attaches "within a decade" to the 1871 launch, saying the first service started "within a decade." That doesn't make sense, and it cuts the phrase off from the expansion it is meant to describe. Choice D puts no punctuation between the two independent clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: 긴 동격구 뒤에 놓인 절 경계를 찾는 2단계 판단을 요구한다. 학생은 경계를 찾고, 도입구가 어느 절에 붙는지도 문맥으로 확인해야 한다. C는 세미콜론을 쓰지만 위치가 틀린 함정이다.

g.passage: In 2021, a stainless steel footbridge built by the Dutch firm MX3D—a structure "printed" by robotic arms that deposited molten metal one thin layer at a time—was installed over a canal in Amsterdam. Sensors embedded in the bridge's frame continuously record strain, vibration, and temperature______ the data feed a "digital twin," a computer model that researchers use to predict how the printed steel will age.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Sensors ... record strain, vibration, and temperature"는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "the data feed a 'digital twin'"도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 따라서 두 독립절을 세미콜론으로 연결한 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 등위접속사 and로 절을 잇는 점은 그럴듯하지만, and 바로 뒤에 쉼표를 찍어 주어 "the data"를 불필요하게 떼어 놓았고, 표준 형태라면 and 앞에 쉼표가 와야 한다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Sensors ... record strain, vibration, and temperature," make up an independent clause, and the words after it, "the data feed a 'digital twin,'" make up another one, with its own subject and verb. A semicolon is the right way to join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it's a run-on sentence. D seems reasonable because it uses the conjunction "and," but the comma comes right after "and" and needlessly cuts off the subject "the data." The standard form would put the comma before "and."
g.design: The opening sentence contains a long dash-set appositive, and the blank follows a list that ends in "and temperature." Because the list's own "and" makes the sentence look already joined, careless readers may pick a comma or no punctuation. They have to see that "the data feed" starts a new independent clause.

g.passage: Biologist Rosalind Achterberg spent three summers tracking alpine bumblebees (Bombus alpinus) on Norwegian mountain slopes, where the insects forage among low-growing flowers that bloom for only a few weeks each year. Her data revealed a surprising pattern ______ colonies nesting near melting snowfields produced more new queens than did colonies nesting on drier, sun-exposed ground, likely because the meltwater kept nearby flowers producing nectar later into the season.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Her data revealed a surprising pattern"은 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 내용은 그 '놀라운 패턴'이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명하는 또 다른 독립절이다. 독립절 뒤에서 앞의 내용을 구체화하는 독립절을 이을 때는 콜론이 적절하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 'and that'으로 시작하는 절이 무엇과 병렬되는지 앞에 짝이 없어 구조가 맞지 않는다. D는 that절이 pattern을 수식하는 관계절처럼 보이지만 that 뒤 절이 이미 완전해 관계절이 될 수 없고, 동격절로 읽더라도 pattern 뒤에 동격 that절을 쓰는 것은 문장을 어색하게 만들어 콜론만큼 관습에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Her data revealed a surprising pattern," form a complete independent clause, and what follows is another independent clause that explains what that surprising pattern was. When a second independent clause specifies or elaborates on the first, a colon is the right punctuation, so C is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B adds "and that," but there is no earlier "that" clause for it to be parallel with, so the structure doesn't work. D could look like a relative clause modifying "pattern," but the clause after "that" is already complete, so it can't be a relative clause. Even if you read it as an appositive clause, "pattern that" fits the sentence less clearly than the colon, which correctly sets up the explanation.
g.design: 긴 지문 속 독립절 뒤에서 구체화 절을 잇는 경계 판단이다. 쉼표 접합, 병렬 없는 'and that', 그럴듯한 'that'절 등 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답과 비교하게 했다.

g.passage: In Mirela Vos's novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, the widowed innkeeper Agathe Brühl keeps a careful record of every traveler who passes through her village. One entry, written on a night of heavy snow, describes a young surveyor who arrived without luggage and refused to give his ______ the next morning, Agathe found the guest room empty, its bed untouched and its window open to the frozen road.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "One entry ... refused to give his name"은 독립절이고, 뒤의 "the next morning, Agathe found the guest room empty..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 접속사만 써서 "his name and the next morning"이 하나의 목적어처럼 읽히며 두 절이 부적절하게 이어진다(run-on). A는 접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 "and"와 도입 부사구 "the next morning" 사이를 잘못 끊는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "One entry ... refused to give his name," is an independent clause, and so is the text after it, "the next morning, Agathe found the guest room empty...". You can join two independent clauses with a semicolon, so D is correct. B joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses "and" with no punctuation, so "his name and the next morning" at first reads like a single object, and the two clauses run together. A puts an unneeded comma after "and," which wrongly separates the conjunction from the introductory phrase "the next morning."
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 관계절(who arrived without luggage and refused...)을 두어 절 경계를 흐리게 했고, 빈칸 뒤 도입구 'the next morning,'가 쉼표 선택지를 그럴듯하게 만든다.

g.passage: Along the arid coast of northern Chile, where rain may not fall for years, some communities draw water from a dense marine fog known locally as camanchaca. Large mesh panels stretched between wooden poles—structures that residents call atrapanieblas, ______ capture tiny droplets from the drifting fog, and the collected water trickles down into storage tanks below.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어 'Large mesh panels' 뒤에 대시로 시작된 비필수 동격 삽입구가 'fog catchers'에서 끝나고, 이어서 본동사 'capture'가 온다. 대시로 연 삽입구는 대시로 닫아야 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표로 닫아 대시와 짝이 맞지 않는다(삽입구 내부 쉼표와 혼동 유발). C는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사 'capture'를 분리하여 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. D는 닫는 부호가 없어 삽입구가 본동사와 구분되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "Large mesh panels" is followed by a nonessential appositive that opens with a dash and ends after "fog catchers." After that comes the main verb, "capture." An element that opens with a dash has to close with a dash, so A is correct. B closes the appositive with a comma, which doesn't match the opening dash. The comma that already appears inside the appositive makes this mistake easy to miss. C uses a semicolon, which would separate the subject from its verb "capture" and leave the first part without an independent clause. D gives no closing punctuation at all, so the appositive runs straight into the main verb.
g.design: The blank comes at the end of a long appositive that sits between the subject and the verb. The appositive already contains a comma, and the comma option (B) looks plausible. To get the answer, students have to find where the dash-opened appositive ends and then link the subject to its verb.

g.passage: In the 1840s, the Lowell Offering, a literary magazine written entirely by young women employed in the textile mills of Lowell, Massachusetts, gave many readers their first glimpse of factory life from the workers' own perspective. Its contributors, most of whom had left farms in rural New England to earn wages of their ______ the drudgery of twelve-hour shifts and the novelty of financial independence in essays, poems, and sketches.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "Its contributors"이고 본동사는 빈칸 뒤의 "described"이다. 그 사이의 "most of whom ... their own"은 비제한적 관계절이므로 앞의 쉼표와 짝을 이루는 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못하고, C는 "and"를 넣으면 주어 "contributors"에 맞는 본동사가 남지 않는다. D는 마침표로 끊어서 앞 문장에는 본동사가 없고 뒤 문장에는 주어가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "Its contributors," and its main verb is "described," which comes after the blank. The words between them, "most of whom ... their own," form a nonessential relative clause. That clause opens with a comma, so it needs a matching comma to close it, which makes B correct. A uses a semicolon, which cuts the subject off from its verb, so the part before it is not an independent clause. C adds "and," which leaves the subject "contributors" without any main verb. D uses a period, so the first sentence has no main verb and the second has no subject.
g.design: 긴 비제한적 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 훑어 읽으면 "own"에서 절이 끝난 것처럼 보이게 했다. 그래서 학생은 수식어를 닫는 쉼표와 절 경계 표시를 구별해야 한다.

c.instruction:

g.passage: At a data center in northern Finland, engineers noticed that the cooling fans, which ran around the clock even during the region's frigid winters, used almost a third of the facility's electricity. The team's fix, a redesign that cost less than replacing the fans with newer models, was surprisingly simple______ ducts that pulled cold outside air directly across the server racks took over the fans' job entirely.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 삽입구 "a redesign ... newer models"를 걷어내면 빈칸 앞은 "The team's fix was surprisingly simple"이라는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "ducts ... took over the fans' job entirely"도 독립절이다. 뒤의 절이 그 '간단한 해결책'이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞아 보이지만 and 뒤에 쉼표가 불필요하게 들어가 있고, 설명 관계도 제대로 드러내지 못한다. D는 that이 뒤의 절을 종속절로 만들지만 "simple, that ducts..."는 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the interrupting phrase "a redesign ... newer models," the text before the blank is a complete clause, "The team's fix was surprisingly simple," and the text after the blank, "ducts ... took over the fans' job entirely," is also a complete clause. The second clause explains what the simple fix actually was, so a colon is the right way to join them, which makes C correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B looks partly right because it uses the conjunction "and," but the comma after "and" doesn't belong there, and "and" doesn't show that the second clause explains the first. D turns the second clause into a "that" clause, but "simple, that ducts..." isn't grammatical.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구로 주절 경계를 가려 훑어 읽으면 혼동하도록 했으며, 쉼표 하나/쉼표+접속사/종속접속어 오답이 각각 그럴듯한 근거를 갖도록 구성했다.

g.passage: Biologist Ana Ruiz has spent years studying the bigclaw snapping shrimp Alpheus heterochaelis, a small crustacean that stuns passing prey with a jet of collapsing bubbles rather than with its pincer ______ when its enlarged claw snaps shut, water rushes out so fast that a cavitation bubble forms and bursts, producing a loud crack and a brief flash of heat.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "a small crustacean ... rather than with its pincer"는 동격 수식어이므로 빈칸 앞의 "Biologist Ana Ruiz ... studying ..."까지가 하나의 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤의 "when ... water rushes out ..."도 독립절이다. 뒤 절은 거품이 어떻게 생기는지 설명하므로 콜론으로 연결한 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 붙여 표준 용법에 맞지 않는다. C는 and와 when 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣었다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a small crustacean ... rather than with its pincer" is an appositive, so everything before the blank is one independent clause. The text after the blank ("when its enlarged claw snaps shut, water rushes out...") is also an independent clause. Since the second clause explains how the bubble jet is produced, a colon correctly joins the two, so D is the answer. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B puts the coordinating conjunction "and" after a semicolon, which isn't standard. C adds an unnecessary comma between "and" and "when."
g.design: 긴 동격 수식어 때문에 앞부분이 이미 독립절이라는 사실이 가려지므로, 수식어를 넘어 주절을 찾고 뒤 절이 설명 관계라는 것까지 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 오답은 쉼표 단독, 세미콜론+and, 잘못 놓인 쉼표+and로 구성했다.

g.passage: The narrator of Imogen Vale's novel The Lamplighter's Daughter, a widowed schoolmistress who records every visitor to her fog-bound coastal boarding house, rarely comments on her guests ______ she describes their luggage, their mud-caked boots, and the hour at which they ring for tea, leaving readers to infer character from such details.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격구(a widowed schoolmistress ... house)를 지나면 주절의 주어 The narrator와 동사 rarely comments가 이어지고, 빈칸 뒤 she describes ...도 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 접속부사 instead로 연결하려면 앞에 세미콜론, 뒤에 쉼표가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 되며, instead는 접속사가 아니므로 쉼표를 더해도 해결되지 않는다. C는 두 절 사이에 아무 경계 부호가 없어 run-on 문장이 되고, instead가 앞 절을 수식하는 것처럼 읽힌다.
g.explanation_en: Once you get past the long appositive ("a widowed schoolmistress ... boarding house"), you can see that the main clause is "The narrator ... rarely comments on her guests directly." The words after the blank, "she describes...," form a second independent clause. When a conjunctive adverb like "instead" joins two independent clauses, it needs a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so A is correct. B and D join the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice, and adding commas around "instead" doesn't fix this because "instead" isn't a conjunction. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence and makes "instead" seem to modify the first clause.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구가 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓아 절 경계를 찾기 어렵게 했다. 오답은 모두 쉼표 위치나 instead 처리만 그럴듯하게 바꿔서, 세미콜론이 필요하다는 점과 접속부사 뒤 쉼표 규칙을 함께 판단해야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

g.passage: The Okavango Delta in northern Botswana, one of the few large inland deltas whose waters never reach the sea, floods at a surprising time of ______ rain that falls on the Angolan highlands in summer takes roughly four months to flow south, so the delta swells to its greatest extent during the region's dry winter.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격 삽입구를 지나 'The Okavango Delta ... floods at a surprising time of year'로 끝나는 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'the rain ... takes ... so the delta swells ...'도 독립절이며 앞 절의 '놀라운 시기'를 설명한다. 따라서 설명을 이끄는 콜론을 쓴 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 연결 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 'which'가 관계절을 만들지만 뒤에 'takes'의 주어 'rain'이 이미 있어 관계사가 들어갈 자리가 없으므로 문법이 깨진다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
g.explanation_en: Once you get past the long appositive, the part before the blank, "The Okavango Delta ... floods at a surprising time of year," is a complete independent clause. The part after the blank, "the rain ... takes roughly four months ... so the delta swells ...," is also an independent clause, and it explains why that timing is surprising. A colon correctly introduces an explanation like this, so B is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C adds "which," but the clause after it already has its own subject ("rain") for "takes," so the relative pronoun has no role and the sentence falls apart. D runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, which is a run-on sentence.
g.design: A long appositive between the subject and verb hides where the first independent clause ends. The distractors are plausible: A looks natural with its comma, and C uses a relative pronoun that seems to connect the clauses.

g.passage: In 1889, reformers Jane Addams and Ellen Gates Starr opened Hull House, a settlement house in a crowded immigrant neighborhood on Chicago's Near West Side______ within a decade, its residents were running a kindergarten, a public bathhouse, and evening classes for factory workers.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격구(a settlement house ... Near West Side)로 끝나지만, 문장의 주절 "Jane Addams and Ellen Gates Starr opened Hull House"는 그 앞에서 이미 완성되어 있고, 빈칸 뒤 "within a decade, its residents were running..."도 독립절이다. 독립절 두 개를 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 알맞으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 등위접속사 and를 쓰긴 했지만 두 긴 독립절을 이을 때 필요한 쉼표가 없다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ends with a long appositive (a settlement house ... Near West Side), but the main clause, "Jane Addams and Ellen Gates Starr opened Hull House," is already complete before it. What comes after the blank, "within a decade, its residents were running...," is also an independent clause. A semicolon is the right way to join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B uses the conjunction "and" but leaves out the comma that should come before it when it joins two long independent clauses. D puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: A long appositive comes before the blank, so it's easy to miss where one clause ends and the next begins. The student has to see that both sides are independent clauses before choosing the punctuation. B looks partly right because it uses a conjunction, and A looks natural with its comma, so the student has to compare them carefully to rule them out.

g.passage: In 2019, engineers at a Danish manufacturer tested a new kind of wind-turbine blade—one molded from a recyclable thermoplastic resin rather than the thermoset epoxy found in most commercial blades______ and found that the prototype withstood the equivalent of two decades of bending stress in only a few months of laboratory trials.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "one molded ... blades"는 "blade"를 설명하는 비필수 동격 삽입구이며 대시로 시작했으므로 대시로 닫아야 한다. 그래야 주어 "engineers"의 동사 "tested ... and found"가 자연스럽게 이어지므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표도 삽입구를 닫을 수 있다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫아 부호가 서로 맞지 않는다. B의 세미콜론은 독립절 사이에만 쓰는데 "and found..."는 주어가 없는 동사구라 독립절이 아니다. C는 부호를 쓰지 않아 삽입구가 닫히지 않으므로 "found"가 "blades"에 이어지는 것처럼 읽힌다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "one molded ... blades" is a nonessential appositive that describes "blade." Because it opens with a dash, it must also close with a dash, so D is correct. Closing it this way lets the compound verb "tested ... and found" connect back to the subject "engineers." A might seem reasonable because commas can also set off an appositive, but it closes a dash-opened interruption with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match. B is wrong because a semicolon must join two independent clauses, and "and found..." is a verb phrase with no subject of its own. C leaves the interruption unclosed, which makes it look as if "found" goes with "blades."
g.design: I put a long appositive opened by a dash between the subject and the second verb of a compound predicate. To answer, students have to find where the appositive ends and see that the punctuation must match the opening dash.

g.passage: The bdelloid rotifer Adineta vaga, a microscopic freshwater animal whose lineage has persisted without males for tens of millions of years, survives repeated drying by entering a dormant state______ when water returns, the animal repairs its fragmented DNA within hours, sometimes incorporating genes from bacteria and fungi in the process.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격구를 걷어내면 'Adineta vaga ... survives ... dormant state'와 'when water returns, the animal repairs ...'가 각각 독립절이므로, 두 독립절을 연결하는 세미콜론인 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 'which'가 관계절을 시작하지만 뒤에 'the animal repairs'라는 완전한 절이 와서 관계대명사가 들어갈 자리가 없다. D도 'that'이 관계절을 만들지만 같은 이유로 관계대명사 that이 받는 빈 자리가 없어 문법에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Once you set aside the long appositive, you can see two independent clauses: "Adineta vaga ... survives ... a dormant state" and "when water returns, the animal repairs ...". A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses, so A is correct. B joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C starts a relative clause with "which," but what follows is already a complete clause ("the animal repairs its fragmented DNA"), so "which" has no role to fill. D fails for the same reason: "that" would start a relative clause, but nothing is missing from the clause after it.
g.design: 긴 동격구로 주절 구조를 가리고, 빈칸 뒤 부사절 'when water returns,'가 종속절처럼 보여 쉼표나 관계사로 이어도 될 듯한 착각을 유도했다. 정답을 고르려면 주절을 확인한 뒤 빈칸 뒤도 독립절인지 판단하는 두 단계가 필요하다.

g.passage: In Mara Ellison's novel The Lantern House, the narrator describes Mrs. Penhallow, a housekeeper who has served the Ashcombe family for nearly forty years and who still wears the black mourning dress of a long-dead mistress. Each night she carries every key to the manor on a single iron ring______ she trusts no one else, not even the young heir newly returned from London, to unlock the shuttered east wing.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Each night she carries ... ring"과 빈칸 뒤 "she trusts no one else ... east wing"은 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 중간의 삽입구 "not even the young heir newly returned from London"에 주의를 빼앗기지 않고 절의 경계를 찾아야 한다. B처럼 세미콜론을 쓰면 두 독립절이 올바르게 연결된다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 등위접속사 and를 쓰긴 했지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 어법에 맞지 않는다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("Each night she carries ... ring") and the words after it ("she trusts no one else ... east wing") each form an independent clause with its own subject and verb. Don't let the interrupting phrase "not even the young heir newly returned from London" distract you from finding where one clause ends and the next begins. Choice B uses a semicolon, which correctly joins the two independent clauses. Choice A links them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. Choice C includes the conjunction "and," but the comma after "and" is unnecessary and breaks the convention. Choice D puts no punctuation between the clauses, which makes a run-on sentence.
g.design: To find the clause boundary, students have to read past a long appositive and an inserted phrase. The distractors are a comma splice, a version with a conjunction but an extra comma, and a run-on, so students must compare the options before eliminating them.

g.passage: Along the coast of northern Chile, where some weather stations have recorded almost no rainfall for decades, the plants of the lomas ecosystem survive on an unusual water source. Dense banks of fog, known locally as camanchaca, drift inland from the Pacific and condense on leaves and spines. Researchers studying these fog oases near the town of Alto Patache have found that the fog's arrival is highly seasonal, peaking in the cooler winter ______ the plants have adapted accordingly, timing their growth and flowering to coincide with the months of heaviest moisture.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Researchers ... have found that the fog's arrival is highly seasonal, peaking in the cooler winter months"와 빈칸 뒤 "the plants have adapted accordingly..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로, 두 절을 세미콜론으로 연결한 C가 정답이다. A는 등위접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 "and,"가 되므로 문장부호 관례에 어긋난다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접속 오류(comma splice)가 생긴다. D는 which 뒤에 "the plants have adapted"라는 완전한 절이 와서 관계대명사 which가 들어갈 자리가 없으므로 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Researchers ... have found that the fog's arrival is highly seasonal, peaking in the cooler winter months") and the text after it ("the plants have adapted accordingly...") are both independent clauses, each with its own subject and verb. C is correct because a semicolon properly joins two independent clauses. A is wrong because it puts an unnecessary comma after the conjunction "and," so you get "and," with incorrect punctuation. B is wrong because a comma alone can't join two independent clauses, and that creates a comma splice. D is wrong because "which" would have to start a relative clause, but a complete clause ("the plants have adapted") follows it, so the sentence doesn't work grammatically.
g.design: 빈칸이 긴 that절과 분사구 뒤에 놓여 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했다. 문장부호만 잘못된 "and," 그럴듯한 쉼표 접속 오류, 관계절 함정을 오답으로 넣어, 수험생이 두 절을 꼼꼼히 비교해야 답을 고를 수 있게 했다.

g.passage: In 1847 the Railway Clearing House, an organization that coordinated ticketing and schedules among Britain's many competing rail companies, urged every member line to set its station clocks to Greenwich Mean Time ______ within a year, most major lines had complied, although a number of towns kept their public clocks on local "sun time" for decades afterward.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장에서는 긴 동격구 뒤에서 주절이 "Greenwich Mean Time"으로 끝나고, "within a year, most major lines had complied..."가 새로운 독립절로 시작된다. 두 독립절을 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다. C는 관계대명사 which를 넣었지만, 뒤의 절이 완전한 절이어서 which가 문장 안에서 맡을 역할이 없으므로 비문이다.
g.explanation_en: After the long appositive, the main clause ends at "Greenwich Mean Time," and "within a year, most major lines had complied..." starts a second independent clause. To join two independent clauses, you need a semicolon, so D is correct. A uses only a comma to join two independent clauses, which creates a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence. C adds "which," but the clause that follows is already complete, so "which" has no role to play and the sentence becomes ungrammatical.
g.design: I put a long appositive near the start so students have to find where the first independent clause ends. I also added a relative-pronoun option that looks like it fixes the problem and a comma option that is easy to miss when skimming.

g.passage: In 1959, engineers at the Rance estuary in Brittany began planning what would become the world's first large-scale tidal power station. The completed barrage, a 750-meter dam fitted with twenty-four reversible turbines, generates electricity as water rushes in and out with the tides. Its designers faced an unusual challenge: because the estuary's tidal range can exceed thirteen meters, the turbines had to withstand enormous shifts in pressure ______ they also had to keep operating efficiently whether water was flowing toward the sea or away from it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'the turbines had to withstand ... twice a day'와 뒤 'they also had to keep operating ...'는 각각 주어와 동사를 가진 독립절이므로 둘을 올바르게 연결해야 한다. A는 쉼표+등위접속사 and로 두 독립절을 대등하게 연결하며, 'also'가 나타내는 두 가지 과제의 추가 관계와도 맞는다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. C의 while은 문법적으로 종속절을 만들 수 있으나 대조·동시성을 뜻해 'also'로 덧붙이는 두 요구 사항의 관계와 맞지 않는다. D의 콜론은 앞 내용을 설명·구체화할 때 쓰는데, 뒤 절은 앞 절을 설명하는 것이 아니라 별도의 과제를 추가하며, 문장 앞에 이미 콜론이 있어 한 문장에 콜론이 두 번 쓰이게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("the turbines had to withstand ... twice a day") and the text after it ("they also had to keep operating ...") are both independent clauses, so they need a correct link. A works because a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "and" joins two independent clauses, and "and" fits the way "also" adds a second challenge. B leaves out any punctuation or conjunction, so it creates a run-on sentence. C is grammatical, but "while" signals contrast or things happening at the same time, which doesn't fit two requirements added with "also." D is wrong because a colon introduces an explanation or elaboration of what comes before it, and the second clause adds a separate challenge instead of explaining the first one. D would also put a second colon in a sentence that already has one.
g.design: 긴 종속절과 앞선 콜론 뒤에서 독립절 경계를 판단하게 했고, 'also'라는 문맥 단서로 while·콜론 오답을 배제하도록 2단계 판단을 요구했다.

g.passage: Ecologist Mariela Ostrovsky studied how the bladderwort, a rootless aquatic plant that traps tiny crustaceans in suction-powered bladders, responds to nutrient-poor water. In ponds low in dissolved nitrogen, the plants produced nearly twice as many ______ in nitrogen-rich ponds, they invested more energy in leafy shoots that capture sunlight.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'In ponds ... as many bladders'와 뒤 'in nitrogen-rich ponds, they invested ...'는 각각 독립절이므로 경계에 세미콜론 같은 강한 부호가 필요하다. 'in contrast'는 두 번째 절을 이끄는 전환어이므로 세미콜론 뒤, 쉼표 앞에 놓인 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 연결해 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 세미콜론을 'in contrast' 뒤에 놓아 전환어가 앞 절에 붙어 버리므로 '질소가 부족한 연못에서 대조적으로'라는 어색한 의미가 되어 대조가 두 번째 절을 이끌지 못한다. D는 부호 없이 두 절을 이어 런온 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("In ponds ... as many bladders") and the text after it ("in nitrogen-rich ponds, they invested ...") are both independent clauses, so they need a strong boundary like a semicolon. "In contrast" is a transition that introduces the second clause, so it should come after the semicolon and before a comma, which makes B correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts the semicolon after "in contrast," so the transition gets stuck to the first clause instead of introducing the contrasting second clause. D uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: 빈칸 뒤 절이 'in nitrogen-rich ponds,'라는 전치사구로 시작해 독립절임을 훑어 읽으면 놓치기 쉽게 하고, 전환어 위치(C)와 콤마 스플라이스(A)를 비교하도록 설계했다.

g.passage: The Okavango Delta in Botswana is unusual among the world's large inland wetlands: rather than emptying into an ocean, its waters spread across the Kalahari Basin and mostly evaporate. Each year, floodwaters from the Angolan highlands take roughly four months to travel the length of the Panhandle, a narrow channel lined with dense papyrus ______ by the time the water reaches the delta's southern edge, the local dry season is already well underway.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞의 긴 동격 명사구 때문에 절 경계가 가려진다. 학생은 동격구가 어디서 끝나는지 확인한 뒤, 그 뒤에 독립절이 이어진다는 점을 파악해야 한다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "a narrow channel lined with dense papyrus swamps"는 Panhandle을 설명하는 동격구이며, 이 동격구로 첫 번째 독립절이 끝난다. 빈칸 뒤의 "by the time ... the local dry season is already well underway"는 또 하나의 독립절이므로, 두 절을 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C의 "which"는 관계절을 시작하지만, 뒤에 이미 주어 "the local dry season"이 있어 관계절 구조가 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a narrow channel lined with dense papyrus swamps" is an appositive describing the Panhandle, and it ends the first independent clause. What comes after the blank, "by the time ... the local dry season is already well underway," is a second independent clause, so you need a semicolon to join the two clauses. That makes D correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B puts the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. C starts a relative clause with "which," but the words that follow already have their own subject, "the local dry season," so the relative clause doesn't work grammatically.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.

g.passage: The Lowell Offering, a monthly magazine written entirely by women employed in the textile mills of Lowell, Massachusetts, first appeared in 1840. Its contributors, many of them farm daughters earning cash wages for the first time______ used its pages to describe factory routines, crowded boardinghouses, and the novels they read during their few free hours.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "many of them farm daughters earning cash wages for the first time"는 주어 "Its contributors"를 설명하는 비필수 삽입구로, 앞에서 쉼표로 열렸으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 주어와 동사 "used"가 이어진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 와야 하지만 앞부분에는 동사가 없어 독립절이 아니다. C의 ", and"는 동사가 없는 주어 덩어리를 동사구와 등위로 연결해 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓는다. D의 대시는 삽입구를 닫는 부호로는 쓰일 수 있지만, 쉼표로 열린 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 부호가 짝을 이루지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "many of them farm daughters earning cash wages for the first time" is a nonessential phrase describing the subject "Its contributors." It opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma, which lets the subject connect to the verb "used." That makes A correct. B is wrong because a semicolon must join two independent clauses, and the part before the blank has no main verb. C is wrong because ", and" links a subject with no verb to a verb phrase, which separates the subject from its verb. D is wrong because, although a dash can close an interrupting phrase, this phrase opened with a comma, and the punctuation on both sides has to match.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 훑어 읽으면 절이 끝난 것처럼 보여 세미콜론이나 ", and"를 고르기 쉽다. 대시 오답은 부분적으로는 그럴듯하지만, 쉼표로 열린 삽입구와 짝이 맞지 않는다는 점을 확인해야 배제할 수 있다.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.

g.passage: When a regional utility in Norway decided to modernize its aging hydroelectric plant, engineers turned their attention first to the intake tunnel. That tunnel—a narrow passage blasted through nearly four kilometers of granite during the plant's original construction in the 1950s______ had developed hairline cracks that allowed water to seep into the surrounding rock and reduced the plant's output.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "That tunnel" 뒤에 대시로 시작된 동격어구(a narrow passage ... in the 1950s)는 같은 부호인 대시로 닫아야 주어 "That tunnel"과 동사 "had developed"가 이어지므로 B가 정답이다. A의 쉼표는 비필수 수식어를 끝낼 수 있는 부호이지만, 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫으면 부호가 짝을 이루지 않는다. C의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 있어야 하는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어+동격어구에 불과하고 뒷부분도 주어가 없다. D의 콜론도 앞에 완전한 독립절이 필요하며, 주어와 동사 사이를 끊어 놓으므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The appositive that describes "That tunnel" opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash too. That way the subject "That tunnel" connects cleanly to its verb "had developed," which makes B correct. A comma can end a nonessential element, but it can't close an interruption that opened with a dash because the punctuation has to match, so A is wrong. A semicolon needs an independent clause on each side. Here the part before the blank is only a subject plus an appositive, with no verb, and the part after it has no subject, so C is wrong. A colon also needs a complete independent clause before it, and it would cut the subject off from its verb, so D is wrong.
g.design: 긴 동격어구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 훑어 읽으면 세미콜론이나 쉼표가 맞아 보인다. 대시가 짝을 이뤄야 한다는 점과 주어와 동사가 이어져야 한다는 점을 모두 확인해야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

g.passage: Along the rocky coasts of the Pacific Northwest, the ochre sea star preys heavily on mussels, preventing them from monopolizing the intertidal zone. In a now-classic experiment, ecologist Robert Paine removed the sea stars from one stretch of shoreline and left a nearby stretch untouched. Within a few years, the number of species in the area where the predators had been removed ______ sharply, as mussels crowded out barnacles, limpets, and algae.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the number'이고, 'of species in the area where the predators had been removed'는 주어를 꾸미는 긴 수식어구이다. 따라서 문장에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하며, 'Within a few years'라는 과거의 일을 서술하므로 단순 과거형 C 'declined'가 알맞다. A 'having declined'와 D 'to decline'은 정동사가 아니어서 문장에 주동사가 없게 된다. B 'were declining'은 시제는 그럴듯하지만, 바로 앞에 있는 복수 명사 'species'나 'predators'에 맞춘 복수 동사이므로 단수 주어 'number'와 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "the number"; the long phrase "of species in the area where the predators had been removed" just modifies it. So the sentence needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and because it describes what happened "within a few years" in the past, the simple past form in C, "declined," is correct. A ("having declined") and D ("to decline") are not finite verbs, so with either one the sentence would have no main verb. B ("were declining") has a reasonable tense, but it is plural, matching the nearby nouns "species" or "predators" instead of the singular subject "number."
g.design: 긴 전치사구·관계절이 단수 주어 'number'와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 정동사 여부 판단과 수 일치 판단을 둘 다 해야 한다. 근처에 있는 복수 명사들 때문에 B가 그럴듯해 보인다.

g.passage: In her 2019 novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, author Imogen Saltash borrows the slow, ornate cadence of Victorian fiction to tell a story set in a present-day coastal town. The book's narrator, an aging archivist who catalogs the letters of a long-dead shipowner, rarely hurries. Instead, the series of digressions about weather, gossip, and faded ink that fills each chapter ______ the reader into the same patient, attentive state of mind that the archivist herself must adopt.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'series'이고, 'of digressions about weather, gossip, and faded ink'와 관계절 'that fills each chapter'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 와야 하므로 D 'draws'가 정답이다. A 'draw'와 C 'have drawn'은 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'digressions'나 'chapter' 근처의 명사에 끌려 복수형으로 쓴 것이라 단수 주어 'series'와 일치하지 않는다. B 'drawing'은 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "series." Both "of digressions about weather, gossip, and faded ink" and the relative clause "that fills each chapter" are modifiers that describe that subject. That means the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, so D, "draws," is correct. A ("draw") and C ("have drawn") are finite verbs, but they are plural forms that would only fit if the subject were the nearby plural noun "digressions," so they don't agree with "series." B ("drawing") is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb and make it incomplete.
g.design: I put a long modifier containing a plural noun ("digressions") between the singular subject "series" and the blank. To get it right, students have to identify the true subject and also see that the blank needs a finite verb.

g.passage: The vast network of underground channels beneath Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula, carved over millennia by slightly acidic rainwater seeping through layers of limestone, ______ the region's only major source of freshwater, since the porous rock allows almost no rivers to form at the surface.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'network'이고, 'of underground channels'와 'carved ... limestone' 분사구는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하며, A가 정답이다. B는 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'channels'나 'layers'에 끌린 복수형이라 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 비문이 된다. D는 정동사이고 시제도 가능하지만 'have'가 복수형이라 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "network." The phrase "of underground channels" and the participial phrase "carved ... limestone" only modify that subject. The blank therefore needs a singular finite verb, so A is correct. B is a plural verb that seems to agree with the nearby plural nouns "channels" or "layers," but it doesn't agree with the actual subject. C is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb. D is a finite verb in a workable tense, but "have" is plural and doesn't agree with the singular subject.
g.design: Two plural nouns ("channels" and "layers") and a long participial phrase sit between the singular subject and the blank. To get the answer, students have to find the real subject and also see that the blank needs a finite verb.

g.passage: Before 1883, most towns in the United States set their clocks by local solar noon, so that noon in Pittsburgh arrived several minutes after noon in Philadelphia. For railroad companies, this patchwork was a serious problem. The sheer number of local times, which by some estimates exceeded fifty across the major rail networks, ______ timetables confusing for passengers and dangerous for trains sharing a single track. In November of that year, the railroads adopted four standard time zones, a system that towns gradually accepted.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'number'('The sheer number of local times')이며, 그 뒤에 긴 관계절이 삽입되어 있으므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하다. 지문은 1883년 이전의 과거 상황을 서술하므로 과거형 B 'made'가 수와 시제 모두 맞다. A는 과거 시제지만 복수형이므로 바로 앞의 'times'나 'fifty'를 주어로 착각하게 만드는 오답이다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다. D는 복수형인 데다 현재완료 시제라서 과거 서술과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "number" ("The sheer number of local times"). A long relative clause separates it from the blank, but the blank still needs a finite verb that agrees with that singular subject. The passage describes the situation before 1883, so the past-tense B, "made," fits in both number and tense. A uses past tense, but "were" is plural, which tempts you to treat "times" or "fifty" as the subject. C is a participle, so it would leave the sentence without a main verb. D is plural and also in the present perfect, which clashes with the past-tense narration.
g.design: 긴 비제한 관계절이 단수 주어와 빈칸을 분리하고, 주어 바로 뒤에 복수 명사(times)와 숫자(fifty)가 있어 수 일치를 놓치기 쉽다. 이 문제를 풀려면 수 일치를 확인한 뒤 과거 시제 문맥도 확인해야 한다(두 단계 판단).

g.passage: Inspecting large bridges for damage once required crews to dangle from ropes and examine steel and concrete by eye. Today, on Denmark's Storstrøm Bridge, a network of vibration sensors embedded in the concrete piers, along with the machine-learning software that interprets the sensors' readings, ______ engineers to detect hairline cracks months before they would become visible to a human inspector.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "a network"이고, "of vibration sensors embedded in the concrete piers"는 이를 꾸미는 수식어이며, "along with ... software ..."는 삽입구이므로 주어의 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. 또한 문장에는 정동사가 필요하고 "Today"는 현재 시제를 나타내므로 단수 현재형인 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 바로 앞의 "sensors"나 "along with" 구문 때문에 주어를 복수로 착각한 형태로, 단수 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. D는 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되므로 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "a network." The phrase "of vibration sensors embedded in the concrete piers" only modifies it, and "along with ... software ..." is an interrupting phrase that does not change the subject's number. The sentence also needs a main verb, and "Today" signals present tense, so the singular present-tense verb in C is correct. A and B are plural forms. They trap readers who treat "sensors" or the "along with" phrase as the subject, so they don't agree with the singular subject. D is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb, so it wouldn't be a complete sentence.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'The fungus gardens'(복수)이고, 'cultivated ... colony'와 which가 이끄는 긴 관계절은 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 이 주어에는 정동사가 필요하므로 복수 현재형 D가 정답이다. A와 B는 정동사 형태이지만 빈칸 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'pulp'(또는 'colony')에 맞춘 단수형이라서 복수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 불완전한 문장이 된다.

g.passage: In 1844, a group of weavers and artisans in Rochdale, England, opened a small shop on Toad Lane that sold flour, butter, and sugar at fair prices. g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'The principles'이고, 'drawn up by the members of this cooperative society'와 'including the practice...' 같은 긴 수식어구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있다. 따라서 복수형이면서 1844년 이후의 과거 사건에 맞는 정동사 'were'가 필요하므로 정답은 C이다. A는 시제는 맞지만 바로 앞의 단수 명사 society나 practice에 수를 맞춘 단수 동사여서 틀렸다. B 역시 단수형이며, 'soon'이 가리키는 과거의 완료된 사건에는 현재완료가 어울리지 않는다. D의 분사 'being'은 정동사가 아니어서 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the sentence is the plural noun "The principles." Long modifiers ("drawn up by the members of this cooperative society" and "including the practice...") separate it from the verb. You need a plural finite verb in the past tense to describe what happened after 1844, so C, "were," is correct. A has the right tense, but it is singular because it agrees with a nearby noun like "society" or "practice" instead of the real subject. B is also singular, and the present perfect doesn't fit a completed past event marked by "soon." D, "being," is a participle and not a finite verb, so the sentence would be left without a main verb.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

g.passage: Along the eastern edge of Lake Chad, a shrinking shoreline has exposed a patchwork of seasonal wetlands. Among the plants that colonize these newly dry flats ______ a hardy sedge whose roots trap windblown sand, slowly building low mounds that later shelter other species.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장은 전치사구 'Among the plants ... flats'가 앞으로 나온 도치 구문이므로 실제 주어는 동사 뒤의 단수 명사 'a hardy sedge'이다. 따라서 단수 정동사가 필요하며, 지문이 현재 시제(has exposed, colonize)로 서술되므로 B의 'is'가 맞다. A와 D는 정동사이지만 복수형이라 바로 앞의 'plants'나 'flats'에 잘못 맞춘 것이다(D는 시제도 맞지 않는다). C의 'being'은 분사로서 정동사가 아니므로 문장의 동사 자리를 채울 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: This sentence is inverted because the prepositional phrase "Among the plants ... flats" comes first, so the true subject is the singular noun "a hardy sedge," which follows the verb. You therefore need a singular finite verb, and since the passage is in the present tense ("has exposed," "colonize"), B, "is," is correct. A and D are finite verbs but plural, so they wrongly agree with the nearby nouns "plants" or "flats" (D also shifts the tense). C, "being," is a participle, not a finite verb, so it can't serve as the sentence's main verb.
g.design: To answer, students must first spot the inversion and the true subject, then pick a finite singular verb in the right tense. The plural nouns placed near the blank ("plants," "flats") draw students toward A and D.

g.passage: In 1844, a group of weavers in Rochdale, England, opened a small shop selling flour, butter, and candles at fair prices. The set of operating principles that these weavers drafted, together with the practice of returning profits to members according to their purchases, ______ a template for consumer cooperatives throughout Europe by the end of the nineteenth century.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The set'이고, 'together with ~' 구는 삽입된 수식어이므로 주어의 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. 또한 이 문장에는 아직 정동사가 없으므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 들어가야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. B는 정동사이지만 'were'가 복수형이라 'principles'나 'together with' 구에 이끌린 오류이다. A와 D는 분사 형태여서 문장에 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장을 만든다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The set." The phrase "together with the practice…" is an interrupting modifier, so it does not make the subject plural. The sentence has no main verb yet, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject. That makes C correct. B is a finite verb, but "were" is plural, so it wrongly agrees with "principles" or with the "together with" phrase. A and D are participles, so either one would leave the sentence without a main verb.
g.design: To answer correctly, students must do two things: identify the real subject past a long relative clause and a "together with" phrase, and recognize that the sentence still needs a finite verb. B tempts students with a plural verb, while A and D tempt them with participles.

g.passage: In 2019, engineers at a Dutch startup began testing a floating breakwater made of recycled plastic modules rather than poured concrete. The modules, each roughly the size of a shipping pallet and linked by flexible steel cables, ______ wave energy by flexing slightly as swells pass beneath them, a design that reduces the stress concentrated at any single joint.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The modules"이고, "each roughly the size of a shipping pallet and linked by flexible steel cables"는 삽입된 수식어구이므로 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하다. 따라서 D "absorb"가 정답이다. B "absorbs"는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "pallet"이나 "each"에 끌려 고른 단수형이라 복수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. A "absorbing"과 C "having absorbed"는 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되므로 문장이 완성되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The modules," and "each roughly the size of a shipping pallet and linked by flexible steel cables" is an interrupting modifier, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject. That makes D, "absorb," correct. B, "absorbs," is a finite verb, but it is singular, which makes it tempting if you match it to the nearby "each" or "pallet" instead of the real subject. A, "absorbing," and C, "having absorbed," are participles, so with either one the sentence has no main verb and is incomplete.
g.design: 빈칸이 긴 삽입 수식어구 뒤에 와서 학생은 주어를 찾는 동시에 정동사가 필요한지도 판단해야 하고, 단수형인 "each"와 "pallet"은 함정으로 넣었다. 분사형 오답 2개는 정동사가 필요한지를 시험하고, 단수 동사 오답은 수 일치를 시험한다.

g.passage: The deep-sea anglerfish Ceratias holboelli exhibits an unusual reproductive strategy known as sexual parasitism. Males, which are far smaller than females, bite into a female's skin and fuse permanently to her body. The network of blood vessels that eventually links the circulatory systems of the two fish ______ the male to receive nutrients directly from the female, so that he no longer needs to hunt for food on his own.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The network"이며, "of blood vessels that ... the two fish"는 그 주어를 꾸미는 수식어구일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 정동사가 필요하고, 지문 전체가 현재 시제로 일반적 사실을 서술하므로 A "allows"가 맞다. B는 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "fish"나 "vessels"에 동사를 맞춘 것이라 주어-동사 일치가 틀린다. C도 시제는 말이 될 수 있지만 복수형 "have"라서 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다. D는 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The network." The phrase "of blood vessels that ... the two fish" just modifies that subject. So the blank needs a singular finite verb, and since the whole passage uses the present tense to describe a general fact, A, "allows," is correct. B matches the verb to the nearby plural nouns "fish" or "vessels" instead of the real subject, so the subject and verb don't agree. C's tense could work, but the plural helping verb "have" doesn't agree with a singular subject. D is a participle, so the sentence would have no main verb and wouldn't be a complete sentence.
g.design: 긴 전치사구+관계절이 단수 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 복수 명사(vessels, fish)에 끌리도록 설계했고, 수 일치와 정동사 여부를 함께 판단해야 한다.

g.passage: In Celia Marwood's novel The Rosewood Box, the narrator slowly reconstructs the life of her reclusive great-aunt. The letters that the widowed Mrs. Ashcombe kept hidden beneath her bed, each one tied with a faded ribbon and annotated in her careful, slanting hand, ______ the reader's only trustworthy glimpse of the passionate young woman she once was.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'The letters'이고, 관계절(that ... bed)과 삽입 수식어구(each one tied ... hand)가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있다. 문장에는 정동사가 필요하므로 복수 정동사인 B가 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 단수형이다. 바로 앞의 'hand'나 'each one', 'Mrs. Ashcombe'에 맞춰 고르면 이 오답을 택하게 된다. C와 D는 분사형이라 정동사 역할을 할 수 없어 문장이 완성되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The letters." A relative clause ("that ... bed") and a parenthetical modifier ("each one tied ... hand") come between the subject and its verb. The sentence needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, so B is correct. A is a finite verb, but it's singular. You might pick it if you matched the verb to a nearby word like "hand," "each one," or "Mrs. Ashcombe." C and D are participles, so they can't act as the main verb, and the sentence would be left incomplete.
g.design: 긴 관계절과 삽입 수식어구로 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓았다. 단수 명사가 여러 개 섞여 있어 훑어 읽으면 A를 고르게 된다. 동시에 정동사가 필요한지도 판단해야 하는 두 단계 구조로 만들었다.
